headline: Continued a variance request for 319 Hunt Street; 85 Hunt Street mixed-use development was presented with no vote.
summary: One Neighborhood Builders presented a proposed mixed-use development at 85 Hunt Street, a city-owned property, and members asked questions about rent, parking, sewer capacity, and security. No vote was taken on that project. The application for 319 Hunt Street, which seeks variances to expand a garage, was continued to the next meeting at the applicant's request. Members also approved the July 22, 2026 minutes.
decisions: Approved the July 22, 2026 minutes and continued the August 26, 2026 minutes, by unanimous voice vote.
Continued Application PZB-2026-09Z for 319 Hunt Street to the next regularly scheduled meeting, by unanimous voice vote.

plain_text:
CITY OF CENTRAL FALLS 
                 COMBINED PLANNING AND ZONING BOARD 
 
 
Page 1 of 4 
REGULAR MEETING 
(PUBLIC HEARING) 
Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 6:00 PM 
The Bessette Building (DPW) – 1280 High Street, Central Falls, RI 02863 
 
MINUTES 
I. Call to Order 
Chair Marenzana called the meeting to order at 6:02 PM. 
II. Roll Call 
Chair Marenzana asked for the roll to be called. Mr. Magnone called the roll and the following members 
were present: Kevin Marchand, Ann Peckham, Hugo Figueroa, Dan Klotz, and John Marenzana. Also 
present were James P. Vandermillen, Director; Joshua B. Magnone, Principal Deputy Director; and 
Joseph P. Baxter, Legal Counsel. 
III. Pledge of Allegiance 
Chair Marenzana led the Board in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance. 
IV. Approval of Minutes 
A.  Regular Meeting Minutes of July 22, 2026 
B.  Regular Meeting Minutes of August 26, 2026 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to continue the minutes of August and approve the minutes of 
July. Mr. Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Ms. Peckham. The vote was taken by voice vote, all 
members voted in the affirmative. There were no objections, the motion passed unanimously. 
V. Public Comment 
Chair Marenzana opened the floor to public comment. There were no public comments. 
VI. Old Business 
A.  Pursuant to its local and statutory authority as the Zoning Board, discussion and possible votes on  
      Application PZB-2026-09Z: 
Effuahson, LLC, of 40 Toronto Avenue, Providence, RI, represented by Jones Harris, Applicant 
for 319 Hunt Street (Assessor's Plat 3, Lot 121), proposes to construct an addition to the 
existing principal garage. The Applicant seeks a Use Variance to expand the legal  
nonconforming use and Dimensional Variances from rear-yard setback requirements (Art. IV, 
Sec. 401, R-3 Zone), maximum lot coverage requirements (Art. IV, Sec. 401, R -3 Zone), and 
from the requirements of Art. IV, Sec. 401.1(B) to permit a total open area  of less than 800 
square feet on the subject property. 
Bret Jedele, the Applicant’s attorney, appeared before the Board.
Page 2 of 4 
Mr. Jedele stated the Applicant may pursue an alternative means of developing the property which may 
include pulling this application. Further, Mr. Jedele stated that they are still in the due diligence phase 
and would appreciate the opportunity to continue this matter to next month’s meeting. 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to continue this item to the next regularly scheduled meeting. 
Mr. Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Mr. Figueroa.  The vote was taken by voice vote, all 
members voted in the affirmative. There were no objections, the motion passed unanimously. 
Mr. Jedele thanked the Board. 
VII. New Business 
A. Pre-Application presentation by One Neighborhood Builders  (ONB) for a proposed Major Land  
       Development at 85 Hunt Street (AP 2, Lot 196), a property owned by the City of Central Falls. 
Marc Titchenell, the Applicant’s attorney, appeared before the Board and introduced the project team: 
• Michelle Bleau, of ONB, Director of Real Estate Development 
• Karissa Kuhns, of DBVW Architects, Associate Principal 
• Steve Andrus, of Commonwealth Engineering, Engineer  
• Chris Tarr, of DBVW Architects, Senior Project Manager 
Ms. Bleau appeared before the Board and presented regarding ONB’s ongoing projects in the City, 
involvement in the RFP process for 85 Hunt Street, and ONB’s goals for the project and this meeting. 
Ms. Bleau described the proposed mixed-use development to the Board including the proposed number 
of units, potential commercial opportunities, green space, parking, and amenities. 
Ms. Kuhns appeared before the Board to present the proposed architectural design for the site. She 
guided the Board through the distributed renderings and site plans, explaining the design elements and 
the considerations that informed them. 
Mr. Vandermillen asked if any of ONB’s proposed office space is included in a certain area. 
Ms. Kuhns responded that the area Mr. Vandermillen was referencing is proposed as tenant space. 
Mr. Klotz asked if ONB has a sense of what kinds of commercial opportunities will be available in the 
building. 
Ms. Kuhns deferred to other members of the ONB team. 
Ms. Kuhns continued guiding the Board through the handouts. 
Mr. Marchand asked if parking in the front of the building is proposed for customers and if parking in the 
rear is proposed for residents. 
Ms. Kuhns stated that is correct and provided the respective number of proposed parking spaces in the 
front and rear of the property. 
Ms. Kuhns continued by highlighting some proposed outdoor amenities and encouraged the Board to 
provide any feedback or ideas. 
Chair Marenzana inquired as to what the average rent will be for the proposed units.  
Ms. Bleau responded by describing the breakdown of how many units will be market -rate and deed 
restricted. Further, Ms. Bleau stated some salient facts from market research that ONB performed. Ms. 
Bleau offered to follow up with specific numbers and a breakdown based on the market.
Page 3 of 4 
Mr. Vandermillen asked if there would be a distribution of different unit sizes across the building and 
across income levels. 
Ms. Bleau confirmed that there will be a variety of room counts spread around the building, available at 
different income levels. 
Mr. Vandermillen asked a question regarding API.  
Ms. Bleau responded. 
Chair Marenzana asked if Ms. Kuhn could provide approximately how far away the rail station is from the 
proposed development. 
Ms. Kuhn referred to a handout that explains the approximate distance and travel time by foot or bike. 
Chair Marenzana asked if there is a forecast of how many people that work in Boston would be attracted 
to live at this development due to the proximity to the rail station. 
Ms. Bleau responded by referring to particular aspects of the market study. 
Chair Marenzana stated that he assumes the property will continued to be owned by the City. 
Mr. Vandermillen stated that is an unsettled question. 
Ms. Bleau stated that she assumes there will be a change in title at a later date, similar to another ONB 
project in the City, or a long-term ground lease will have to be put in place. 
Chair Marenzana stated the reasoning behind why he is asking about the market for this development. 
Ms. Bleau acknowledged that there are many elements of the proposal that are based on the market 
study.  
Mr. Figueroa asked a question about sewer capacity.  
Mr. Andrus stated that NBC has provided a letter stating that its interceptors have capacity for the 
proposed sewer flow stemming from the development. 
Mr. Magnone added the City is currently developing a Wastewater Facilities Plan and has performed 
CCTV inspections of various sewer mains throughout the City, including around the area of the proposed 
development. 
Mr. Andrus formally introduced himself and presented to the Board. 
Mr. Andrus described existing site conditions, access to utilities, and acknowledged the environmental 
land use restrictions and the need to keep the site ‘capped.’ 
Mr. Andrus further added that they will be adding a landscape architect to the project soon. 
Mr. Marchand asked if a fire truck can fit into the site. 
Mr. Andrus responded that a fire truck can fit into the site and added that he will continue speaking with 
the fire department to ensure they are satisfied with access. 
Mr. Vandermillen noted that this is a very early presentation and that there will be multiple stages of review 
for this project. 
Mr. Vandermillen also noted that there will be a focus approach on engaging residents and business 
owners in regard to the proposed development of the site. 
Mr. Figueroa asked if more parking can be accommodated on the site. 
Mr. Vandermillen explained that the site’s proximity to public transit qualifies the project for a bonus that 
reduces the required parking below the standard requirement.
Page 4 of 4 
 
Mr. Vandermillen asked about stormwater management on the site. 
Mr. Andrus responded by describing stormwater management that can be done at catch basins, 
acknowledging the need to be thoughtful given the residual environmental contaminants on the site. 
Ms. Bleau noted that ONB is aware of the City’s tree canopy goals and looks forward to discussing how 
the site can help meet those goals once a landscape architect joins the project team. 
Ms. Bleau also noted opportunities for community input on the use of certain areas of the site, lighting 
installations, and the types of murals the community would like to see.  
Mr. Magnone described the City’s combined sewer system and the overflows that can occur during heavy 
rainfall. He asked whether an underground stormwater retention system could be installed to temporarily 
store runoff and gradually release it into the combined sewer system. 
Mr. Andrus and Mr. Magnone discussed various aspects of the existing stormwater infrastructure on -site 
and whether that infrastructure ties into the combined sewer system. Both agreed that sharing more 
information about infrastructure between the City and project team would be helpful. 
Ms. Bleau appeared before the Board again to address the types of commercial opportunities that may 
be available on-site, including healthcare, education, and workforce development opportunities. 
Mr. Klotz commented that community events intended to solicit feedback on developments often have 
low attendance. He asked how ONB plans to encourage attendance and ensure that participants are 
reflective of the community. 
Ms. Bleau introduced Karen Zuñiga, Director of Resident Services for ONB. 
Ms. Zuñiga outlined ONB’s community partnerships and its approach to community engagement. 
Ms. Bleau stated that ONB is excited to share the project with the community. 
Chair Marenzana asked if the Board had any further questions. 
Mr. Marchand commented that he had concerns about security on the site. 
Ms. Bleau stated there will be 24/7 surveillance in terms of cameras and maybe a concierge service. 
Ms. Bleau continued by stating that ONB will start with inclusivity and traditional management practices 
and adjust as necessary. 
Chair Marenzana thanked the project team for the presentation. 
VIII. Adjournment 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to adjourn. Mr. Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Mr. 
Klotz. The vote was taken by voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There were no objections, 
the motion passed unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 7:21 PM.
